text:
Thanks for the video! Your observations line up very closely with my own experience.

I’ve been working quite a lot with Codex lately, including on Ultra, and one thing I’ve definitely noticed is the enormous amount of testing it tends to do. More importantly, though, I recently had Codex build an app more or less from scratch, and unfortunately the end result was basically unusable from a UX perspective.

It technically does a lot, but the interface is completely overloaded. It’s often unclear what the user is supposed to do, what the next step is, or even where to focus. When you first land on the page, you’re simply overwhelmed by everything that’s there.

So it was particularly interesting – and somewhat disappointing – to hear that this seems to be a more general Codex tendency, and that Claude Code apparently doesn’t suffer from it to the same extent.

I really hope OpenAI improves this, because fundamentally I enjoy working with Codex a lot. But especially when using the higher-priced tiers, I’ve definitely been disappointed by this aspect of its behaviour.

text: One-shotting an app is NOT the most efficient method. Try planning the app first. Then work the plan. One-shot features, not apps. Doing this does keep the human in the loop a lot more, but these models are NOT ready to one-shot entire apps unless those apps are extremely simple or you have no real idea of the end product and whatever it produces is fine. Develop apps feature by feature. You'll use fewer tokens and the model will not wander as much. Building a feature at a time allows independent testing of each feature and allows the developer to catch model drift and to adjust if the dev wants to course correct without an entire rebuild and using tons more tokens. Even when models get better at one-shotting apps, you will still need to re-work it again and again because we don't even know everything the app needs or should do. We start with a general idea and refine during development. Trying to one-shot an app skips that in-line-development and is sure to disappoint. Great video though!
